title: Abstract's blanket survival claim omits the headline variant's documented catastrophic failure
quote: pre-registers four falsification criteria, among them the published dev-calibrated CISC protocol as a designated killer baseline, all of which the method survived.
explanation: What raised concern at the desk screen: the abstract's final sentence, read together with 'guarantees sign consistency whenever the plurality-error rate is below one half', presents an unconditional safety story for the variant that carries the abstract's headline number (the label-free variant, credited with 1.000 vs. 0.807 at kappa=-0.6). What I checked: Section VII reports that this same variant, in a paraphrased wrong-majority cell, 'mis-signs, saturates at $\gamma=-2.0$, and scores $0.000$ against an \SC{} floor of $0.340$', that 'None of the four alarms fires', and that 'the guarantee is conditional, the condition is not observable label-free, and the existing diagnostics do not detect its violation'. What remains: the survival claim is literally defensible, because pre-registered falsifier F2 was scoped 'either variant significantly below \SC{} anywhere on the sweep' and the paraphrase cell is post-hoc follow-on work rather than a sweep cell. But that scoping is invisible in the abstract. A program-committee member who reads only the abstract will believe no configuration of the method can score below the majority-vote floor, then discover a 0.000-vs-0.340 collapse in Section VII. This is the failure mode most likely to make an otherwise sympathetic reviewer hostile, because it converts the paper's genuine self-criticism into apparent concealment. The fix is one clause, not new experiments.

Section IX (Experimental Setup) falsifier F2: 'either variant significantly below \SC{} anywhere on the sweep'
TACT-LF 0.000 vs SC 0.340 in the paraphrased wrong-majority cell

missing_evidence: any statement in the abstract that the label-free guarantee is conditional on an unobservable quantity
any statement in the abstract that a documented off-sweep cell drives the headline variant to 0.000 against an SC floor of 0.340 with no alarm firing
explicit scoping of the four falsifiers to the synthetic coupling sweep, so 'survived' is not read as global
allowed_wording: All four pre-registered falsifiers, evaluated on the coupling sweep, survived; a post-hoc paraphrased-wrong-majority cell outside the pre-registered protocol drives the label-free variant below the self-consistency floor with no alarm firing, and is analysed in Section VII.
forbidden_wording: all of which the method survived
guarantees sign consistency (stated without naming the unobservable condition in the same sentence)

title: Contribution list C1-C4 omits the real-trace campaigns, which are the majority of the Results section
quote: This paper frames the problem as estimating one scalar: the \emph{signed} within-item discrimination of the confidence channel, and mapping that scalar, with its uncertainty, to a vote exponent. The contributions are:
explanation: What raised concern: this sentence opens the contribution list, and C1-C4 that follow reference only the synthetic sweep, the analytic map, the impossibility results and the falsification protocol. Real LLM traces appear in none of the four. What I checked, in the source: Results (Sec. V) spans tact.tex lines 248-509 at 2203 words; the three real-trace subsections (Real-trace validation, Confirmatory campaign on harder items, How wide is the addressable stratum?) span lines 357-509 at 1158 words, against 1045 words for the entire synthetic block. So the material absent from the pitch is larger than the material the pitch is built on. Its headline number is the one the paper itself calls the binding constraint: the addressable stratum 'measures $2$--$7.5\%$ of items across five substrates in two domains'. That bound applies to every confidence-weighted voting method, not only to the one proposed here, which makes it the most transferable empirical result in the manuscript. What remains unresolved: a program-committee member reading title, abstract and introduction learns neither that this is the paper's largest experimental block nor that the real-trace evidence is null on accuracy; only Section VII states 'does not extend to accuracy'. This is not a request to add content that appears later - the content exists and is good; the objection is that the pitch is mis-weighted against the paper it introduces, which at a desk screen reads as a synthetic-only submission with a buried disclaimer.

title: No code or data availability statement, although the proof-verification argument is delegated to unobtainable code
quote: Proofs are elementary and pinned by unit tests in the released code (76 tests;
explanation: What raised concern: the manuscript substitutes numerical pinning for full proofs and points the reader to 'the released code'. What I checked: a case-insensitive search of tact.tex for available / github / open source / reproduc / artifact / release / repositor returns only in-body uses of the word 'released' (Sec. IV-B on tested propositions, Sec. V-C, Sec. V-F here, Sec. VI-C on the alarm-fix narrative). There is no URL, no DOI, no repository name, no archive reference, and not even an 'available upon publication' sentence in nine pages, and the IEEEtran preamble contains no availability or acknowledgement block. What remains unresolved: three propositions, a permutation-verified null variance, an empirical-Bayes identity, a link derivation, and a bug-fix narrative that the author offers as evidence of methodological care are all asserted to be verifiable in an artifact the reviewer cannot reach. For a single-author independent submission this is the least recoverable gap in the manuscript, because nothing in the verification chain is externally checkable. A related hygiene point that a reviewer will hit immediately: the stated count is 76 tests, while the checked-in suite at tests/*.py exposes 93 test functions across 7 files, so the number as printed needs either a precise scope or a correction.

title: Discussion contradicts itself and the abstract about whether real-trace validation was performed
quote: Validation on real LLM traces is the remaining step; the cached-trace runner is committed and the prediction is falsifiable
explanation: What raised concern: this sentence closes the first paragraph of Section VII and states that real-trace validation has not yet happened. What I checked: the fourth paragraph of the same section reports 'the measured cost of acting anyway was negative on both real substrates' and cites Table VII, Section V-G/V-H report two completed campaigns on a frozen model, and the abstract states 'Two real-trace campaigns on a frozen model confirm the premise and locate the binding constraint'. Read charitably, the author means that validation of the accuracy *gain* on real traces remains outstanding - which is true and is stated precisely later in the same section ('does not extend to accuracy'). But as written the sentence makes an unqualified claim about the whole real-trace programme and directly contradicts three other places in the paper. What remains unresolved: this looks like a stale survivor from a pre-real-trace draft that was not updated when Sections V-G to V-I were added. At a desk screen an internal contradiction of this kind functions as a signal that the manuscript was not read end-to-end before submission, which discounts the credibility of unrelated numbers elsewhere. The repair is to scope the sentence to the accuracy claim, or delete it because the later paragraph already states the point correctly.

evidence_anchor.text: Section VII paragraph 4: 'the measured cost of acting anyway was negative on both real substrates'
Abstract: 'Two real-trace campaigns on a frozen model confirm the premise and locate the binding constraint'
Sections V-G / V-H (Real-trace validation; Confirmatory campaign on harder items)

missing_evidence: reconciliation between 'validation on real LLM traces is the remaining step' and the two completed real-trace campaigns reported in the same paper
allowed_wording: Real traces confirm the premise and the abstention behaviour; validation of an accuracy gain on real traces remains the outstanding step, and requires a (model, benchmark) pair with a wider addressable window.
forbidden_wording: Validation on real LLM traces is the remaining step

title: 371-word single-paragraph math-dense abstract fills the entire first column; 95-word conclusion is the mirror defect
quote: Written out, the method is a single expression whose exponent reduces to $\gamma=z\sqrt{2+z^2}$
explanation: What raised concern at the presentation baseline: the abstract is one 371-word paragraph and, in the rendered two-column IEEE layout, occupies the whole of page 1's left column before the Index Terms line. What I checked: the rendered PDF confirms the abstract runs from the title block to 'Index Terms' with no break, and the abstract carries inline mathematics throughout - the quoted exponent expression plus $\kappa=-0.6$, $\Dhat=+0.250$, $z=+2.54$ and $p=3.3\times10^{-24}$. IEEE conference style expects a roughly 150-250 word abstract without equations or symbols, precisely because the abstract is what a committee member skims and what indexing services strip. What remains unresolved: the density is not merely a style violation, it is functional - the reader must decode a shrunk-pooled-AUC probit before reaching sentence four, so the paper's actual selling point (the sign of the confidence-correctness association is unrepresentable in every published scheme) competes with notation instead of landing. The mirror-image defect confirms a distribution problem rather than a writing-length problem: the Conclusion is a single 95-word paragraph closing a 9-page paper, while Results runs 2203 words across 6 tables and the Method section that gives the paper its name runs 626. Six keywords is fine and is not part of this finding.

title: Nine pages in IEEEtran conference class with no named track, and a venue-community mismatch with every comparator cited
explanation: What raised concern: the class option declares an IEEE conference submission, and the rendered document is 9 pages (body to page 8, references spilling to page 9) carrying 6 tables and 4 figures. Most IEEE conference tracks cap camera-ready length at 6 pages plus up to 2 purchased pages, or hard-cap at 8; a 9-page submission is rejected mechanically at check-in with no reference to merit. I cannot name the target track because the manuscript does not identify one, so I state the trigger conditionally: if the chosen track's limit is below 9 pages, this is a desk reject before review. The second half of the concern is community fit, and here the manuscript's own bibliography is the evidence: the designated killer baseline CISC is cited as 'Findings of ACL, 2025', and the comparator set (self-consistency at ICLR 2023, adaptive consistency at EMNLP 2023, early-stopping self-consistency at ICLR 2024, rank calibration) is entirely *ACL/ICLR work. The reviewers who can adjudicate a pooled van Elteren Somers' D estimator with item-clustered jackknife standard errors applied to self-consistency voting are drawn from that pool. What remains unresolved: if the length must come down, it must not come out of the Method section, which at 626 words is already the thinnest substantive section in a paper named after its method; the compressible material is the 6-table Results block and the abstract.
